item.title: Senator Moody introduces bill to protect anonymity in crime stoppers rewards
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody rolled out new federal legislation today aimed at helping citizens report crimes while staying anonymous—even when collecting rewards for tips that lead to arrests. During a Crime Prevention Month event in Tampa, Moody gathered with law enforcement officials from across the Tampa Bay region, including Hillsborough County…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody rolled out new federal legislation today aimed at helping citizens report crimes while staying anonymous—even when collecting rewards for tips that lead to arrests.

During a Crime Prevention Month event in Tampa, Moody gathered with law enforcement officials from across the Tampa Bay region, including Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office deputies. She highlighted her push to empower ordinary people to assist police, building on what the FBI recently reported as a historic drop in violent crime nationwide.

"It's vital that citizens are empowered to help fight crime," Moody said, referencing her work creating Florida's **TIPS statewide tip hotline when she served as Attorney General. Her new bill, she said, would let people collect reward money for helping officers make arrests without having to give up their anonymity.

The legislation has backing from major law enforcement groups including the Florida Association of Crime Stoppers, Florida Sheriffs Association, the Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association, and the National Fraternal Order of Police. According to Crime Stoppers officials, the bill addresses a federal reporting requirement that can complicate anonymous cash reward payments—a challenge that's emerged over 50 years of operating tip programs across multiple states.

item.title: Santa Rosa Health Dept. Offers Walk-In Tetanus Shots Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County is hosting a walk-in tetanus vaccination clinic Thursday, October 15, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. at their Milton office, 5527 Stewart St. No appointment is needed. The clinic comes as the region continues recovery efforts following recent hurricane activity. Tetanus, caused by bacteria found in soil…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County is hosting a walk-in tetanus vaccination clinic Thursday, October 15, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. at their Milton office, 5527 Stewart St. No appointment is needed.

The clinic comes as the region continues recovery efforts following recent hurricane activity. Tetanus, caused by bacteria found in soil and the environment, can enter the body through wounds — particularly cuts from contaminated debris. The infection classically affects the jaw and neck muscles, leading to the common name "lockjaw." Hurricane cleanup work significantly increases exposure risk through minor cuts and puncture wounds that might otherwise go unnoticed.

Residents of Santa Rosa County who need a tetanus booster or primary vaccination are encouraged to attend. Those with questions about the tetanus vaccine can contact the health department at 850-851-8929 or visit the CDC's vaccine information page for more details.

The Jack Brewer Foundation will provide 1,000 prepared meals on a first-come, first-served basis beginning at 6 p.m. at Jernigan's Landing. item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is hosting a community meal distribution event tonight to assist residents affected by Hurricane Isaias. The Jack Brewer Foundation will provide 1,000 prepared meals on a first-come, first-served basis beginning at 6 p.m. at Jernigan's Landing.

Each vehicle is limited to four meals, and distribution will continue while supplies last. The city has outlined a specific traffic route to manage the flow of vehicles: drivers should enter via Canal Street, continue to Pine Street, and proceed to Willing Street to access the pickup location. Personnel will be on hand to direct traffic and assist with the distribution.

For more information, residents can contact the City of Milton at (850) 983-5400.

Rock band Matchbox Twenty is bringing their 30th Anniversary Tour to the Gulf Coast next summer. According to a Live Nation announcement, the group will perform at The Wharf Amphitheater in Orange Beach on August 5, 2027.

The tour marks a milestone year for the rock band, which formed in the mid-1990s and has built a devoted fanbase through hits like "3AM" and "Bent." Specific ticket information and on-sale dates have not yet been announced.

The Wharf Amphitheater is Orange Beach's premier outdoor music venue and regularly hosts major touring acts. More details about the concert are expected to be released by Live Nation in the coming weeks.

item.title: BRACE Seeks Donations for Long-Term Isaias Recovery in Escambia, Santa Rosa
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — As Northwest Florida moves from emergency response into longer-term Hurricane Isaias recovery, BRACE is asking residents and businesses to help support recovery efforts in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties. Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies serves as the lead local agency for Emergency Support Function 15, which…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — As Northwest Florida moves from emergency response into longer-term Hurricane Isaias recovery, BRACE is asking residents and businesses to help support recovery efforts in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies serves as the lead local agency for Emergency Support Function 15, which coordinates volunteers and donations following disasters.

The organization also serves as a fiscal agent for disaster-recovery efforts in the two counties and leads their Long-Term Recovery Groups.

Those groups bring together nonprofit organizations, churches, businesses, government agencies and other community partners to address needs that can remain long after the immediate emergency ends.

“Disaster recovery does not end when the storm passes,” BRACE CEO Dr. Nick Jackson said. “Families may continue dealing with damaged homes, debris, lost belongings and other needs long after the immediate emergency is over.”

BRACE says financial contributions are particularly useful because recovery needs can change over time and funding can be directed toward identified gaps not covered by other resources.

Residents can contribute through the BRACE Hurricane Recovery donation page.

BRACE will continue coordinating with emergency managers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties as recovery needs are identified.

item.title: Santa Rosa Expands Hurricane Supply Distribution; Six PODs Operating
item.dc:creator: news6334

The newest locations are Navarre High School and Tiger Point Community Center in Gulf Breeze . Both are scheduled to operate from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. daily until…
item.content:encoded:
SANTA ROSA COUNTY, Fla. — Santa Rosa County has expanded its Hurricane Isaias supply distribution operation, with six Points of Distribution now serving residents from Navarre to Jay.

The newest locations are Navarre High School and Tiger Point Community Center in Gulf Breeze.

Both are scheduled to operate from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. daily until further notice, providing water, ice and tarps.

Four additional PODs are operating at Hickory Hammock Baptist Church in East Milton, Bray-Hendricks Park in Jay, King Middle School in Milton and Munson Air Strip.

The northern sites are distributing MREs, water, ice and tarps.

Additional feeding operations are also underway through the Red Cross, Salvation Army and other disaster-relief organizations.

Residents needing physical help cleaning up storm damage can also contact Crisis Cleanup at 800-451-1954.

Volunteer organizations may be able to assist with roof tarping, fallen-tree removal, debris cleanup and other storm-related needs. Assistance depends on volunteer availability.

item.title: Southwest Drives Record September Traffic at Santa Rosa Airport
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County's airport saw its busiest September on record, driven largely by strong performance from Southwest Airlines, according to reporting by The Press Democrat. The airport's traffic surge reflects broader travel demand during the month, with Southwest capitalizing on the market. The carrier's performance stands in contrast to Alaska…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County's airport saw its busiest September on record, driven largely by strong performance from Southwest Airlines, according to reporting by The Press Democrat.

The airport's traffic surge reflects broader travel demand during the month, with Southwest capitalizing on the market. The carrier's performance stands in contrast to Alaska Airlines, which has expanded its flight schedule at the airport but is currently operating with lower load factors — meaning more empty seats relative to a year ago.

The mixed results highlight shifting dynamics in regional air service, with some carriers gaining ground while others adjust to demand patterns. Santa Rosa County's airport continues to serve as a key transportation hub for the region.

item.title: Santa Rosa Schools Plan Wednesday Reopening; Several Campuses Damaged by Isaias
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, Fla. — Santa Rosa County public schools are preparing to reopen Wednesday, although officials say individual campuses could remain closed if they cannot safely accommodate students. Superintendent Karen Barber said the district was directed by Gov. Ron DeSantis and the Florida Department of Education to work toward a Wednesday reopening.…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, Fla. — Santa Rosa County public schools are preparing to reopen Wednesday, although officials say individual campuses could remain closed if they cannot safely accommodate students.

Superintendent Karen Barber said the district was directed by Gov. Ron DeSantis and the Florida Department of Education to work toward a Wednesday reopening.

Several campuses suffered damage during Hurricane Isaias.

Milton High School sustained significant damage to its gymnasium, including a partially removed roof. Hobbs Middle School sustained damage to a multipurpose room, while Gulf Breeze High School was damaged along its main hallway.

Jay High School and Jay Elementary also sustained storm damage, and some schools experienced water intrusion.

The challenge extends beyond school buildings.

Santa Rosa County transports approximately 16,000 students, and some normal bus routes may remain obstructed by debris. County crews are making additional passes along school-bus routes, and the district says alternate routes may be necessary.

Barber has asked parents to supervise children traveling between their homes and bus stops because storm debris and other hazards remain.

DeSantis said Monday that the state expects most Panhandle schools to be operating Wednesday.

Escambia County has not yet announced whether all of its campuses will reopen Wednesday. Superintendent Keith Leonard said Monday the district was evaluating power, building damage and bus-route safety and could consider shared campuses or other temporary arrangements if individual schools cannot reopen with the rest of the district.

item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has lifted its precautionary boil water notice for most of mainland Escambia County and all of Perdido Key, according to a Tuesday announcement from the utility.

However, some addresses remain under the precautionary notice. Customers still affected will be notified by door hanger, ECUA said. Pensacola Beach also remains under the precautionary boil water notice, though the utility expects that restriction to be lifted by Wednesday, October 14.

ECUA did not immediately detail which specific addresses remain under the notice or the reason for the initial precautionary measure. Affected customers are urged to watch for door hanger notifications or contact ECUA for status updates on their service area.

item.title: Florida Democratic Party Targets Big Tech Spending in State Legislative Races
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Democratic Party is calling out what it describes as a coordinated effort by tech billionaire Scott Banister to defeat Democratic state legislative candidates through a newly formed political committee. According to a statement released Tuesday, First Amendment LLC — funded entirely by Banister, a PayPal co-founder and major investor…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Democratic Party is calling out what it describes as a coordinated effort by tech billionaire Scott Banister to defeat Democratic state legislative candidates through a newly formed political committee. According to a statement released Tuesday, First Amendment LLC — funded entirely by Banister, a PayPal co-founder and major investor in artificial intelligence companies and data center infrastructure — plans to spend more than half a million dollars opposing Democrats in Florida's state races.

Democratic leaders framed the spending as retaliation against their opposition to large-scale AI data centers and surveillance technology expansion in Florida. Party Chair Nikki Fried characterized the effort as part of a larger Republican strategy to allow tech companies to build data centers across the state without adequate public input or oversight. "Florida Republicans are handing our neighborhoods over to Big Tech for massive data centers and turning our streets into a Flock-powered surveillance state," Fried said in the statement.

Democratic lawmakers including Senate leader-designate Tracie Davis and House leader-designate Christine Hunschofsky pledged to maintain their opposition to data center development without stricter environmental and utility rate protections. Senator Brian Nathan specifically called for a moratorium on new data center projects, citing concerns about pollution, rising utility costs, and community impact.

The political spending represents an escalation in a debate that has increasingly divided Florida lawmakers over how aggressively the state should pursue data center and AI infrastructure investment. The Democratic Party's statement suggests the issue will be a significant point of contention in the coming legislative elections.

Impersonating a police officer is a felony in Florida. The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: ECUA Lifts Boil Water Notice for Most of Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The advisory remains in effect for Pensacola Beach, which is expected to be lifted by Wednesday pending confirmation that water quality meets…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has lifted a precautionary boil water notice for most of mainland Escambia County and all of Perdido Key following Hurricane Isaias, officials announced Tuesday.

The advisory remains in effect for Pensacola Beach, which is expected to be lifted by Wednesday pending confirmation that water quality meets applicable requirements.

However, residents at specific addresses across multiple streets must continue following boil water precautions until ECUA announces the notice has been lifted for their locations. The affected areas span St. Regis Drive, Conifer Road, Springhill Drive, Valley Drive, Edendale Lane, and numerous other streets throughout the county. (see below)

"Some mainland addresses remain under the precautionary boil water notice," ECUA stated in the release. "Customers at the addresses listed below must continue following the boil water notice until ECUA announces that it has been lifted for their location."

Affected customers will receive door hanger notifications informing them of their status. ECUA emphasized the importance of continued vigilance in areas still under the advisory.

"Customers whose addresses remain on the list should continue to follow boil water precautions until ECUA issues an official notice lifting the advisory for their location," the authority stated.

The utility authority is working to restore normal water service and ensure system safety following the hurricane's impact. Residents can monitor progress through multiple channels.

"ECUA will provide updates as additional areas are cleared," officials said. The authority is encouraging customers to visit ECUA.fl.gov and follow ECUA's social media channels on Facebook (@ECUA.Official) and Instagram (@ecua_fl) for the latest information.

ECUA expressed gratitude for community cooperation during the recovery period. "ECUA appreciates the community's patience and cooperation as crews continue working to restore normal water service and ensure the safety of the water system following Hurricane Isaias," the release concluded.

Residents uncertain about their status should check the official ECUA website or contact the utility directly for clarification on their specific address.

item.title: Santa Rosa Damage Assessment Underway as County Seeks FEMA Individual Assistance
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, Fla. — Santa Rosa County is about halfway through its assessment of Hurricane Isaias damage as officials work to determine whether the county can qualify for FEMA Individual Assistance. County Administrator Brad Baker said Tuesday that preliminary assessments have identified roughly 30 destroyed homes, more than 100 homes with major damage…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, Fla. — Santa Rosa County is about halfway through its assessment of Hurricane Isaias damage as officials work to determine whether the county can qualify for FEMA Individual Assistance.

County Administrator Brad Baker said Tuesday that preliminary assessments have identified roughly 30 destroyed homes, more than 100 homes with major damage and 161 with minor damage.

The assessment was approximately 50% complete when Baker spoke with NewsRadio 92.3 Tuesday morning.

The numbers are being provided to the Florida Division of Emergency Management as they're collected.

Baker said both state and county damage thresholds must be met before the governor can seek the federal declaration necessary to make FEMA Individual Assistance available to residents.

“We're knocking our area out so we can give them all the numbers that they need and then hopefully the governor can advocate on our behalf for a disaster declaration,” Baker said.

FEMA Individual Assistance has not been approved for local hurricane victims.

Residents are being encouraged to report damage to their primary residences through their county's damage-reporting system. Those reports help officials document the scope of the disaster.

Commercial damage is assessed through a separate process.

Baker said he's confident the county will qualify for public assistance, which helps governments recover eligible disaster expenses, but Individual Assistance requires separate thresholds.

item.title: More Than 43,000 FPL Customers Remain Without Power in Escambia, Santa Rosa
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Power restoration continues across Northwest Florida Tuesday morning, with the number of FPL customers without electricity falling by more than half since Monday afternoon. As of 10 a.m. Tuesday, Florida Power & Light reported 24,620 customers without power in Escambia County and 18,580 in Santa Rosa County , for a combined…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Power restoration continues across Northwest Florida Tuesday morning, with the number of FPL customers without electricity falling by more than half since Monday afternoon.

As of 10 a.m. Tuesday, Florida Power & Light reported 24,620 customers without power in Escambia County and 18,580 in Santa Rosa County, for a combined 43,200 outages.

That compares with 91,230 customers without service across the two counties at 2 p.m. Monday.

Escambia and Santa Rosa remain the two biggest challenges in FPL's Hurricane Isaias restoration operation. Other heavily affected Northwest Florida counties are much closer to full restoration.

FPL has said it expects to reach approximately 95% restoration by the end of Tuesday, although some customers in the hardest-hit areas may take longer because of extensive damage and limited access.

Customers still without power can now receive personalized estimated restoration times through FPL's outage system.

The timeline is different for customers of Escambia River Electric Cooperative, particularly in rural Santa Rosa County. EREC has warned that some of its hardest-hit territory may not reach 90% restoration until Thursday.

Residents whose neighbors have regained electricity but whose homes remain dark should make sure their outage has been reported directly to their utility.

item.title: National Democrats pour $7.5M into Florida races ahead of November election
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: National Democratic groups are significantly increasing their financial commitments to Florida's competitive races as the November election approaches, according to a statement from the Florida Democratic Party. The Democratic Attorneys General Association announced a $5 million investment supporting José Javier Rodríguez's campaign for Florida…
item.content:encoded:
National Democratic groups are significantly increasing their financial commitments to Florida's competitive races as the November election approaches, according to a statement from the Florida Democratic Party.

The Democratic Attorneys General Association announced a $5 million investment supporting José Javier Rodríguez's campaign for Florida Attorney General, while the Democratic super PAC American Bridge has spent $2.5 million in Florida's U.S. Senate race as part of a broader nationwide effort. Together, the commitments total at least $7.5 million in new resources flowing into the state.

Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried characterized the national investment as validation of grassroots organizing work in the state. "National Democrats are putting real money behind Florida because they see what we've been building on the ground for the last three years," Fried said in a statement, citing recruitment of more than 1,000 candidates and efforts to flip competitive seats.

The investments underscore how Florida has become a focal point for both parties in the lead-up to November's general election, with national organizations viewing several races in the state as competitive and potentially winnable.

item.title: Century DCF Comfort Center Offers Free Supplies, Showers for Hurricane Relief
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Florida Department of Children and Families Comfort Center has opened in Century to help residents recovering from hurricane damage. The facility, located at the Century Business Center at 150 East Pond Street, is distributing essential supplies at no cost, including food, diapers, feminine hygiene products, tarps, and cleaning materials. The…
item.content:encoded:
A Florida Department of Children and Families Comfort Center has opened in Century to help residents recovering from hurricane damage. The facility, located at the Century Business Center at 150 East Pond Street, is distributing essential supplies at no cost, including food, diapers, feminine hygiene products, tarps, and cleaning materials.

The center also operates 24/7 shower and laundry trailers on site, providing critical services for residents whose homes may lack running water or functional utilities following the storm. The relief effort is part of DCF's broader disaster response network across the state.

Residents in need can visit the center during operating hours. The availability of these basic services reflects the ongoing recovery challenges many North Escambia families face as they work to restore their homes and lives.
